justifications.durability: tests/test_worker_git_guard.py:514 launches the composed guard as a real subprocess under the current interpreter with -I and a live synthesised pointer, asserting a cross-checkout commit is denied with exit 2; the import that guard depends on, renamed in a scratch checkout, reddens exactly that case as I reproduced (1 failed, EXIT=1), and tests/test_worker_git_guard.py:481 asserts the composed command resolves to a checkout carrying reckon/worker_git_shim.py. The two corrected docstrings are prose and no test pins their wording, so a future reword could silently contradict the guard again; that is the only durability gap and it is inherent to a prose deliverable.
justifications.evidence: the gate tests/test_worker_git_guard.py records 59 passed EXIT=0 at 03f13dacc in the reviewed manifest, and my independent head arm over the same file reproduces it (59 passed EXIT=0), against a base arm of 57 passed EXIT=0 at 6205b507b, so head adds two passing cases and no failure; the declared negative control renaming the shim import to a missing module reddens the isolated deny case exactly as recorded (1 failed, EXIT=1), reproduced here in review-negative-control.log.
justifications.fit: both docstrings are written in their module's own voice beside the clauses they correct — the __init__ package docstring narrows "each module" to "most modules" and names worker_git_guard as the exception, and the _git_guard_group docstring amends its own standard-library-only claim — and no plan, sprint or ticket identifier appears in the changed source, the two test names describe the behaviour, and both commits carry a subject with a body.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/hooks/install.py:222 and reckon/hooks/__init__.py:3 now say the worker git guard must run from a reckon checkout because it imports reckon.worker_git_shim from that checkout, putting it on sys.path itself, and that a standalone copy would raise on that import and fail open; I read the mechanism in reckon/hooks/worker_git_guard.py:51-53 (_CHECKOUT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] inserted on sys.path) and :354 (the shim import), and confirmed a missing shim exits 1 rather than 2, i.e. fail open, so the prose matches the code.
justifications.scope_discipline: commits 5ee19a727 and 03f13dac touch exactly the two docstring files, the test file and the evidence fragment, all inside the node's declared write paths; no plan meta line changes and no figure path is written.
